But as for the personnel who were senior, whom I didn't discuss at that assembly session, my answer would be the same.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correction to the transcript. It's not the Serbian Radical Party but the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But my question was a bit different. In dividing positions in the MUP --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I didn't stand up in time for the first time he asked the question, but I'll stand up at this time and say it's a leading question. The witness didn't answer it the first time and we object to it being asked a second time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who came to the positions that belonged to the Serbian people in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the position which, in the distribution of positions between the HDZ, the SDA, and the SDS belonged to different ethnic groups, members of those ethnic groups would be assigned. It couldn't be otherwise. In our former Ministry of the Interior, all the people I know were professionals, even before the national parties ever emerged, and some of them later were assigned to these positions on behalf of the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday on page 79, a document was displayed which you said was incomplete, and it says that five Muslims were in Ljubinje and one in Nevesinje. What is missing from that report? Which areas and how much territory is not covered by that report?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of Republika Srpska if we are talking about Ljubinje, Kalinovik, and did you say Nevesinje?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ljubinje and Kalinovik. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's part of the old Herzegovina. So it's a minor part compared to the total of six or seven centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the share of Muslim population in Kalinovik and Ljubinje?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that these were municipalities with a majority Serb population, but I don't know the exact percentage. It was a considerable Serb majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, did you attend the parade of the MUP unit in Banja Luka on the 12th and 13th May, 1992, after the assembly session?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did not attend the session of the assembly, but I came to the parade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you speak at that parade?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we just see D414, which is the transcript, and we can even play it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the stance taken by Mr. Zupljanin and yourself regarding the work of non-Serb policemen at that centre?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we upload it. Yes, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't see how this arises out of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Hmm. I don't know ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will say it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes -- just collapse this document first, for the moment. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, how does this arise from the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, it was challenged that the MUP also employed non-Serbs; that is to say, Croats and Muslims. This document is needed for us to see how things really were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I -- I just stood up to make sure that -- that Mr. Karadzic wasn't going any further on his explanation. But let's see -- I say we can see the documents and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But I wonder whether Mr. Karadzic can ask questions before he put this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought I have already put the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the stance taken by Mr. Zupljanin and by this minister, the witness, towards the work of non-Serbs in the police?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I expressed my position through my order. That means that all the employees of the ministry from the former Bosnia-Herzegovina who are located in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina should stay in their jobs as employees of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska. That was my desire. And if it had materialised that way, things would have been much better.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At that rally, was there any discussion about the presence of Muslims and Croats in the police?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly there was a large number of them. I don't know the exact number, but I know that all who had previously worked in the ministry, non-Serbs who had worked previously in the ministry, were still there. I can't give you the exact number, and I don't want to speculate.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To avoid wasting time, we won't play the video. That's 945 -- 494, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at page 1. Is this what you said or answered?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you say here that although things are apparently satisfactory, caution is necessary?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, when I accepted the position of minister, in my platform, I announced that I would work strictly professionally and within my jurisdiction and powers. I was talking about the results achieved by the ministry in terms of security in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page; line 32 and 33, which is the speech of Mr. Zupljanin. [In English] English too. [Interpretation] He says here: These people who addressed the MUP were asking desperately and begging that problems should be solved. Could we see the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'll read it out to you: "I am really happy to be able to stress here that about 85 per cent of authorised officials, including many members of other ethnicities who remained to work in this centre of security services, and they are still among our ranks." Do you remember what he said, this particular passage; and do you remember that he received an ovation from 50.000 people?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I see that page again in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thirty-two, 33.

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I hadn't seen this passage before. Now I confirm that Stojan Zupljanin, indeed, said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it mean -- what does it mean that authorised officers signed the solemn declaration? And were the non-Serb employees --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be asked not to start answering before the question is over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer. Interpreters couldn't hear you because of the overlap.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The question was not finished either.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... [Microphone not activated] yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the question was not interpreted in full either.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I asked: What does it mean that authorised officials were signing solemn declarations and does it mean that other employees, non-Serbs, had to do it too, if they were working in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, leading. He could have simply stopped with his first part of this question but then he suggests an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking only why only authorised officers are singled out here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are there employees in the MUP who are not authorised?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You're answering too quickly. Please put a pause before you start answering the question. Yes, could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Ministry of the Interior, there are not only authorised officers. There's an entire administration dealing with legal and -- and other affairs. There is the fire brigade, et cetera. Only authorised officials who are officers make a solemn declaration when signing an employment contract.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now can we go to the following page, please. Look at the first sentence. Read it to the full stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we're not hearing any interpretation. Could you indicate what passage you are reading from?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: First two lines in Serbian. And in -- in English, it's fifth, sixth, and seventh from the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Minister, what he said at that time? And how did you and the people react to that claim?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember what he said, and what I'm reading here confirms everything that he said. It is true that after that he was greeted by a round of applause by everybody who was present in the square. There were thousands of them. There were a lot of people present in the square in front of the building where Stojan was speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you give us a summary - it doesn't have to be precise - of how many Croats and Muslims worked in other institutions, those who were not part of that report?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to tell you that there were two stages in that. Initially a significant number of Muslims and Croats remained working in the Ministry of the Interior. Mr. Delimustafic sent a dispatch which created a problem. The president of the Crisis Staff of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Ejub Ganic, and himself invited all the members of Muslim ethnicity who were still working in the MUP to leave it because they would not have any rights because we were deemed to be illegal, and then people started leaving, but some of them remained working in the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska. I can't give you the percentages of various ethnic groups. But, as I say, it was then that the problem was created and when the two persons I have just mentioned sent them that dispatch, they started leaving the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you were shown a report drafted by Mr. Zupljanin and sent to you. In that report, it was stated that the military brought civilians to the MUP, those of Croat and Muslim ethnicities, and left them there for the MUP to look after them. Why were civilians brought from somewhere? Where were they brought from; and why was it the army who did that?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be pure speculation if I told you anything about those specific situations. I know what Stojan Zupljanin said. However, if you're asking me who was supposed to look after those people under such circumstances, it should have been the civilian protection that existed within the Ministry of Defence that had to look after the civilians to move them from such places where they were threatened, and that was all in keeping with international laws. They were the -- a part of the same organisation as the military, the Ministry of Defence. I don't know how things were in reality. I just told you what I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The document number is P1097, that was Zupljanin's document. What did he do? Was his reaction appropriate or in appropriate when he informed you about the problem?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the remit of his competencies, he couldn't deal with a problem that should have been dealt by the military. That's why he presented the problem at the collegium and then I informed you about those things that we couldn't deal with. I invoked your authority and asked you to resolve the problem as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honours. Leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Already answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the only way, Your Excellencies. This document was taken as if it was against me, although Zupljanin actually acted within the law. I just want to establish whether he did things by the book or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just continue without leading.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. We didn't hear your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You have just told us that you informed me about all that.

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The prime minister and yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up D3966.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the document? It was drafted on the 8th of August. It was drafted on your behalf by the assistant for the police, Mr. Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. That document was issued on the 17th of July, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. When we have this document before us, let's please look at the following, please -- page. Look at the page. I don't want to read it because everybody can read. Is this the position of the Ministry of the Interior? Is this its attitude towards the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's collapse the document. You could put it without presenting the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the attitude of the Ministry of the Interior towards the civilian population of any ethnicity? What was the treatment according to the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see from a number of my orders that my position was clear. In -- in all of them, I emphasised clearly that those problems should be dealt with energetically. That would be that. I saw the document, actually, I wanted to say something about it as well, but then you collapsed it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back and see the second page of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you whether that document reflects what was your position and the position of the ministry. Zupljanin's dispatch was sent on the 20th of July, and the document before us was issued on the 8th of August.

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a product of all of our activities. Mr. Kovac was the assistant for policing, and all information about the police went through him. In this document, he clearly advocates the application of rules and regulations in treating with the civilian population, which was in keeping with all of our orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Minister, the Prosecutor showed you a piece of information -- or a report from the public security station in Ilidza. The document number is P6639. Yes, I apologise. You mentioned your own order issued on the 17th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to call up 65 ter 5299. No, no, not -- not this one. 65 ter 5299. The transcript reflects a good number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A week after Kovac's document, could you please tell us, you issued this order to a chief or, rather, was it sent to all the CSB chiefs? What did you want to do with it?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To all the CSBs for the attention of chiefs personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What did you want to achieve with this order?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order is quite unequivocal and clear. If you want me, I can read it: "I again order," which means that either one or several orders had been issued before that, "that all employees of CSBs, SJBs, and their organisational units, that is all the employees of the MUP, in their treatment of prisoners of war and civilian population-refugees act strictly according to law, within the remit of the MUP and according to laws of war and international conventions which regulate the subject matter."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to intervene. The -- the interpretation is good, but in the last sentence, it says "the persons who perform regulations." Does it mean violate regulations?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, violate regulations, and act contrary to our own rules and regulations and international laws regulating this subject matter, irrespective of whether they were civilians or members of the MUP or the military. Immediately collect information and documentation and file a criminal report to the competent prosecutor's office. This is my order and it is dated 17 August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the population that you sought protection for? Who were prisoners of war and refugees in our war?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who could they have been? The position [as interpreted] signed, the entire civilian population, all the refugees.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D4280, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that that was a repeated order, which means that you had issued previous orders to that effect.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 5294.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you co-operate with the military with regard to those crimes and compliance with the law?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The co-operation between the military and the MUP went through the security organs in the army. We worked together on elucidating crimes and capturing the perpetrators. It was war time and that group could comprise of civilians and soldiers. In order to avoid a situation where they would not be punished because of the confusion of competencies we decided to work together and that we should process those people according to our competencies.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go to the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this your signature, is this your document?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you sent it to the Main Staff, the administration for intelligence; right?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the second paragraph it says that you again underlined the need to co-operate and act in co-ordination with military organs to prevent and detect a rising number of crimes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D4281, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, yesterday on pages 71 and 73, you were reproached -- the establishment of war units and then that you ordered that the territory should be controlled against terrorist groups. According to our law, who is supposed to control the territory --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In a statement of emergency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please repeat your question, Mr. Karadzic. But he was never reproached for that. Yes, please continue. Interpreters didn't hear your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, according to our laws, who is it who controls a conflict zone and who controls the rest of the territory?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a state of emergency and in a state of war, the entire territory is divided into zones under the authority of the corps, of course. Military organs are duty-bound to deal with crimes that fall within the jurisdiction of military prosecutor's offices and military courts, which means that they performed the tasks that are performed by the Ministry of the Interior in peacetime. As for the MUP, within those zones, if something concerns exclusively the remit of the Ministry of the Interior, they will deal with that if it falls within the jurisdiction of civilian courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know or, rather, did you receive from me certain instructions and guide-lines on the functioning of defence forces and state organs in a state of war or a state of emergency?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that these guide-lines were discussed by the government, but you'd need to show me a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please take a look at D3111.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: To save time, I'm anticipating that this will be leading. The question should be, What were those instructions or guide-lines, before Mr. Karadzic shows him a document and ask him to confirm whether that, in fact, was the guide-lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He confirmed that he received the instruction from the president. And what was the problem showing that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I was just anticipating, Your Honour, a leading question that was going to be of the nature that I'm concerned about. That there could have been another question in there regarding what those guide-lines were about before putting the document to the witness and saying, you know, Is this the guide-line I issued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We cannot rule on that without hearing the question. Yes, please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, what was the intervention of the Presidency and the president based on? The behaviour of the MUP, instructions about the behaviour of the MUP, what was that based on?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You acted within your authority. In this case, the constitution and the Law on National Defence. That is to say, in addition to the fact that you are the Supreme Commander of the armed forces, you also establish the number of members of the active-duty force and reservists of the ministry, and also you issue general instructions, in terms of what the ministry should do in cases of a state of emergency or a state of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From the preamble, can you tell who it was that prepared this proposal that I passed?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Articles 5 and 7, Official Gazette, et cetera, et cetera. The proposal of the government of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the president of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina is passing the following guide-lines on tasks, modes of action, and functioning of defence forces of state organs and subjects in the field of economy and social activities, Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, in a state of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, have you ever heard of Variants A and B, and have you ever acted in accordance with them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Does it arise from the cross-examination, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Excellencies, I wish to establish, on the basis of what the authorities acted. And he was the authority during the first year, preeminently so. But I can give up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, do you remember what was prescribed as an obligation of the Ministry of the Interior in these guide-lines?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can remember in general terms. But you can show it to me. I cannot go into detail. You can show it to me and then I can confirm. It's been a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. I'll show that you --

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what it was like, whether the ministry received any tasks about documenting crimes; and, if so, against which population?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can just say that I remember that a constant topic was the struggle against all perpetrators of crimes. And also uncovering these crimes, regardless of the victims and perpetrators involved.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have page 4 in Serbian. It would be chapter 3. And then it will be easier to find it in English too. Now, it is being recalled here, quite literally, this is in the imperative: What the ministry will do. Could we have the Serbian and the English turned to the next pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, the very end, this last paragraph, what does it speak of; and what is the civilian population that is referred to there?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the last paragraph in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, on the top.

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the last one or do you mean the one on the top?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The last one in three.

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have three. I have 11, 12, 13, and up here I have this paragraph that doesn't have a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Oh. All right.

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Ministry of the Interior and its organisational parts shall collect and process data and material on the crimes committed and genocide over the civilian population."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it specified there which civilian population, which ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It goes without saying, there is just one civilian population, the civilian population throughout. And, of course, it goes without saying, it is irrespective of ethnic background, all of those who live in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Minister --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But what does this genocide refer to, Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, my opinion is, Your Honour, that this refers to what should be done, that if that does happen, then information should be collected about that too. So this is a lasting task. It doesn't have to do with a concrete event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Which genocide does this refer to? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do not see -- well, you see, there are tasks there. There is no specific genocide here. It says here they will work on collecting and processing data and material on crimes committed and genocide over the civilian population. That is to say, if it is committed, then it is the duty of the Ministry of the Interior to collect documents. That is my understanding of it now and that was my understanding of it then. Had it been anything concrete, it would have been stated concretely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. I leave it at that. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 71 of yesterday's transcript, the Prosecutor said that you had made some plan with war units and you invoked the law. What were the legal and strategic bases? What was the attitude of the Yugoslav state towards a state of emergency and a state of war, imminent threat of war? What were the legal obligations involved?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as this document was concerned, I only acted within the regulations that were in force at that time in that area. The regulations that had to do with this subject matter are the Law on National Defence and the strategy of All People's Defence and Social Self-protection. And all organs at the time had to have plans for possible preparations for defence. I acted on the basis of the law. There were also inspections taking place at the time. If an organisation - even an economic organisation - did not have that kind of plan, they would be punished for not having one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show in e-court 1D8801. In English, please -- oh, it's not ... 1D49070, could that be shown on half of the page for purposes of having English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, can you tell us, can you confirm that this had been very recent at the time, passed in 1987?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have the Serbian on the left-hand side. Who passed this document?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the Presidency of -- the Presidency of Yugoslavia. The president, Lazar Mojsov, as far as I can remember. This is just my recollection. But I think it is an approximately correct or totally correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, this goes beyond the scope of my cross-examination. I never went into these kind of issues. This document is from well before the conflict, 1987, and I'm not sure if I mentioned the word TO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You mentioned the war unit, war organisation. You dealt with it. And then -- and then you dealt with the involvement in combat operation and specialist operation. So this may be related to that issue. We'll see how it evolves. Please -- please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have the translation of all the pages in English but could we have the next page in both languages -- or, rather, in Serbian, the next two pages, or the next one. [In English] In English, too, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Lazar Mojsov --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably page 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, was this document in force in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The constitutional law on the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina said at the time that all the regulations of the former Yugoslavia would be in force in the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina but that is the -- the way it was in the other parts, I think, too; in the Croatian part and the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next page in Serbian. And I kindly ask the Trial Chamber for their indulgence and patience, if they could hear the minister read a paragraph, something that President Tito said about national defence. The next page in Serbian, and we do not have a translation for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, could you please read this out slowly.

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Work related to All People's Defence and social self-protection are being carried out and increasingly so, if I may put it that way. Through work and parallel to work, they become therefore a part of regular everyday activities and work tasks."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Working people and citizens, self-managers, organised themselves, their defence and self-protection, in work communities and social political community and only indispensable joint activities shall be transferred to social communities through specially organised institutions, like the Yugoslav People's Army and the security services. In that way, in practice, we ensure the socialisation of the defence function. That is, in other social -- that is, alienated in other social systems from the working people. This is in practice the implementation of the Marxist concept of the armed people. Signed Tito."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear Mr. Karadzic's question or the answer. This was the sight translation of the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the interpreters didn't hear your last comment, or your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The question was: Who signed this? Who said this?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the words of Josip Broz Tito, the president of the former Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. And All People's Defence and social self-protection were built on that basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This document, did it mean -- or, rather, did it provide certain tasks to the Ministries of the Interior as well?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean. This, what is written, or the strategy?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I mean the strategy.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have page 15 in English. We don't have it in Serbian, unfortunately. Not everything has been uploaded. Maybe it's 16 or 17 in e-court, and maybe 15 is written on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read out the lower part to you. I'm going to read it out slowly, Minister: "The organs of internal affairs and state and public security services, as specialised professional organs of social self-protection, shall be active in an area caught up in an emergency situation, and beyond, applying appropriate means and methods suitable" -- [In English] Please, I ask interpreters to interpret: "Suitable for these specialised services and duties and powers prescribed by the constitution and the law -- the power prescribed by the constitution and the law, and special powers they receive from the relevant organs in emergency situations. "Relying on the overall system of social self-protection, in emergency situations, these organs will remove any existing incidents and prevent others which may represent a threat to security."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page, please. I won't read anymore. I just want to display it. In paragraph 1, it says: "The basic tasks of these organs and services of internal affairs" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before -- what is this about?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, the Prosecution made an objection to the effect that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no, no, I'm talking about this document. We saw some provisions and -- and this seems to be a speech. What is this document about? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we saw the first page. It was written by the Presidency of Yugoslavia in 1987. This is a legal obligation, stipulating how various services must act. We have seen before certain guide-lines in a shorter form, but this is the strategy of defence for the entire country and this is a list of the tasks for the Ministry of the Interior --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no. Probably Mr. Robinson could assist us. Page 1, page 2, 3, is -- is signed document about strategy of All People's Defence. And from page 4 on, it seems like a transcript or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: This is the way we received it, Mr. President, so we believed it was an integral document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And no B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: We may have received the B/C/S at a different time but we received the English in this form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you have no idea what this document is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: As far as we can tell, this is a document setting forth the strategy for the All People's Defence by the authorities of the former Socialist Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may add, Your Excellencies. These are partial translations. The original has 400 pages. These are translations only of passages from the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Translation of what, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show the first page, please. It's a book. It's a document, a legal enactment. Could we see the first page in Serbian as well. [In English] Right half. [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, in Serbian, the specification of the publisher is more complete. The issuing authority is the Federal Secretariat for National Defence, and it was endorsed by the Presidency of Yugoslavia as the Supreme Commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you assist us as to what this document is about? What we are seeing before us? Can you show page 4 and 5 in B/C/S to the witness. Yes, having seen this document, can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can tell you my understanding. I understand this as a well-developed Law on National Defence, in case the country has to be defended. This provides much more -- much broader comments, how every participant in the defence should act, including businesses, companies, not only the army, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you remember having seen this book, or read this book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, I remember the book. In the spirit of my work, as far as the ministry is concerned, I read the other parts, but I didn't memorise them, as I did the part that concerns the Ministry of the Interior. But basically it's described more briefly in the Law on the Interior and the Law on National Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then move on to page 15, 16. We've seen this already. [In English] Next page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We've read this, Minister. It begins with the tasks of the Ministry of the Interior and I'll deal with one more passage here. The second paragraph: [In English] "The organs and services of internal affairs shall take all measures and actions from their field of work in closest co-operation with other subjects of social self-protection. They shall establish a direct and constant operative and working connections with the committees for All People's Defence and social self-protection," and so on and so on. [Interpretation] Let's just see third paragraph: [In English] "In an emergency, by prompt, energetic, and efficient actions and activity, committees of All People's Defence and social self-protection must provide and be responsible for the following: Directing and co-ordinating measures and activities in the implementation of common goals and tasks of All People's Defence and social self-protection; operative and political monitoring and assessment of the situation stimulating the activities of organs of self-management organisations and communities, social, political, and other social organisations and socio-political communities, in the struggle against the causes of the emergency and to eliminate them; prompt and efficient action of the joint system of defence protection." [Interpretation] Could we see the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you continue, we can collapse the B/C/S because we don't have B/C/S page. Zoom in, in English.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here it begins about the Territorial Defence. But the first paragraph is still under the heading MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So, did the law assign certain tasks to the Ministry of the Interior and did you act in accordance with this? Or did you offend these provisions by establishing war units?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must confess, I did not locate this passage which relates to defence preparations in the Ministry of Interior. But it says here that on the ground, in the event of a war, how to create Crisis Staffs. They can be called differently, but that would be an organ in that territory capable of functioning independently until communication is established with the state authorities at the top. That's how I understood it. But, as far as I understand, that's the way it's also written. And all these agencies are duty-bound to make these preparations during peacetime, to have them ready in the event of war. And there were even inspectors and inspections checking whether these preparations have indeed been made, and all those who did not have these plans in place were fined very seriously.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 73 of yesterday's transcript, it was held against you that you had assigned a task to control the movements of sabotage terrorist groups.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 16. [In English] Not next. Previous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure it was an issue of translation, but Mr. Olmsted never held against Mr. Stanisic about that. I just want it noted. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the break, I'll read just a short passage. Line 3 says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you put -- please -- please proceed. We'll take a break after this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "The basic task of the organs and services of internal affairs are as follows: By applying preventive measures and actions to provide protection for important social and governmental [sic] institutions, buildings, and other property from sabotage and terrorist attacks and other criminal acts [sic] at the centre of an emergency and in the general area ..." [Interpretation] So this protection against sabotage terrorist action, under whom was it?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the regular job of the Ministry of the Interior, falls combat against terrorist group, terrorist actions, if they are targeting civilian buildings and civilian population. If they target military installations or troops or anything that falls under the army, that would be the task of the military security and other organs within the army. And I said, in one of my orders, as far as terrorist groups are concerned, that the ministry within its jurisdiction can deal with, we will use our units and deal with them. But that's strictly the civilian aspect of that work.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tendered the first three pages to be MFI'd. And out of this text, I tendered the second page, where the list is complete. The third page. And pages 15, 16, 17. Those that have been shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we mark those pages for identification? Do you have any objection, Mr. Olmsted?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: We don't necessarily object to this being admitted into evidence but with confirmation that those were in fact the pages shown to the witness. I'm not quite sure about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. So we'll mark those pages pending the translation. And later on you may raise the issue if you have some issues with respect to authenticity or whatever. So we'll mark those pages for identification. We'll assign a number for that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D4282, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll take a break for 45 minutes, Mr. Karadzic. We'll resume at 22 past 1.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.38 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, just one small evidentiary matter. In the last session, D4280 was admitted into evidence and I would just like to note for Your Honours that it is, at least in content, the same document as D469 which I referred to during cross-examination. I think one is in the form of a dispatch and another one is signed by the witness, but I just wanted to note that for -- for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll ask the Registry to make a cross-reference to each other. Yes, please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, you were asked about the division of MUP in two different MUPs and also about that telegram which supposedly resulted in the division. And you spoke about the results of the conference. However, the results of the conference was just the legal background. What were the reasons for us to approach Cutileiro and the European community with that request? What were the requests to have another MUP? What were the reasons for that request?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you expect from me. As for the political part, I don't know what the reason was because I didn't participate in the negotiations so I don't know. But I know when Yugoslavia disintegrated the legal system in Bosnia-Herzegovina and all the other republics of the former Yugoslavia in -- disintegrated as well, so it was in the interests of every ethnic group in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina to find a solution that would lead to a normal life in a state but within the framework of ethnic entities. That would be just my reasoning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How did federal units in Yugoslavia deal with that situation? Did they have their on police forces and what about other European states with multi-ethnic composition? Who has the right to have a police force?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every republic had its own police force and within the framework of the former Yugoslavia, and there was an umbrella organisation which was the police force of the federal state of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the eve of the conference when we still had a joint police force were there any problems? How did that MUP function as a whole? Not just the police force but the MUP as a whole? Were there any problems at all?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in late 1999 -- or in the course of 1991, the security situation in the territory of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina gradually deteriorated. All the laws that were applicable in Bosnia-Herzegovina were actually tied to federal regulations. As Yugoslavia disintegrated, the systems in the republics disintegrated as well. And as a result of that, the security situation worsened in the entire territory and we had to find a solution to overcome the crisis that was imminent and that was already in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: After the inter-party agreement, did the MUP continue to function harmoniously and did the parties comply with the agreements reached between them?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The parties tried to appoint people to various positions according to the agreement but there -- a lot of problems in the Ministry of the Interior. The situation prevalent in the territory of the entire republic reflected on the ministry because the Ministry of the Interior started to lose its basic function as a ministry, and it started to deal -- and it -- and it actually ceased dealing with tasks within its remit, and that made the situation more and more complex by the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were shown a document in which you said that it was not the Serbs that the -- were in the process of dividing the MUP but the Muslims. What did you have in mind? What developments did you have in mind when you said that?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian cadre in the Ministry of the Interior of the former Bosnia and Herzegovina mostly insisted on the implementations of laws and regulations which were in effect at the time in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was still in place at that time, so there were grounds on insisting on the application of all the rules and regulations in that area. But it was already clear that the Muslim side did not want to comply with the federal regulations and that its option was to secede from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. And that undermined the legal system in the former Bosnia-Herzegovina. We kept on insisting on certain things. We wanted to comply with all the positive rules and regulations while we were still functioning. That was the only guarantee for the situation to be under control in Bosnia-Herzegovina. If legalities -- not respected in the MUP, what could other citizens do, especially people prone to illegal doings?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to call up 65 ter 8170. This document, which is in e-court is what it is, we need page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 20 April you warn everybody of the need to dispatch daily bulletin. Yes, page 3. This was issued on 9 September 1991. 9 September 1991. This is a -- a press release. Could you please tell us what was publicised here. What was the general public informed about? [In English] Public announcement. This is -- this part belongs with public announcement. [Interpretation] Would you please look at the document and tell us what did you, the Serbian cadre, tell the general public in September 1991? What did you inform the general public about?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only tell you that the text is a true reflection of what we have discussed over the past three days as a problem pertaining to that field of work. People who were admitted were prone to the commission of crimes, people with criminal records; i.e., these official IDs were issued to people who had nothing whatsoever to do with the Ministry of the Interior, who were not employed by the MUP. Already in May -- or, rather, after July 1991, the Green Berets were established as a reserve strength of the special unit of MUP of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina and the commander of that unit was Juka Prazina, and that person had spent at least 15 years in prison, up to then. Obviously we reacted because we feared for our own lives, because if that person could be in command of a unit with a same or similar structure while, at the same time, MUP members actually apprehended him all the time, all we could except was retaliation. Unfortunately, that was the composition of the special brigade of the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the ethnic affiliations of the members of that formation?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were Muslims. Most of them were Muslims and there was also an occasionally Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Look at the fax that was sent on the 9th September, 1991. The document in e-court was not prepared by us, but, still, do you remember when this was announced? I believe that -- we're still talking about the joint MUP; right?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not following what document we are talking about. Fax of when?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: In Serbian, Excellency, this page is dedicated only to this document. In English, it is -- of -- of public announcement. It is a separate document. And above the public announcement should be what is fax -- facsimile, 9 September 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Released through the Ministry of Information of BH.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's dated 1st -- 7th of September, 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: 9th of September, I suppose. So we -- we tender only this page because two other documents does not belong organically to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where can we see 9th of September?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Could page be shifted little bit left -- right. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The date of fax, yes. So it is not attached to the previous document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: It's not the same. It's difference several months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we will admit this page.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D4283, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a reaction heard at the collegium of the Serbian people in September. Were there any discords even before that? How did you deal with those misunderstandings and discords? I'm talking about the functioning of the MUP and the behaviour of the other side.

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I was the secretary of the MUP Sarajevo. I tried, together with my associates, to have the secretariat function in compliance with the law. And, to a certain extent, I was successful in that. But I know that outside of Sarajevo, and at the top of the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina, there were huge problems. It would take me a lot of time to talk about details, and I don't know whether my answers would be -- be really precise. In any case, there were problems, and this letter is a product of all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the Muslim MUP send the Muslim members for training somewhere unbeknownst to Serbs and against the regulation?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina had its training centre in Vrace, in Sarajevo. Irrespective of the fact that that centre existed, it was not the ministry but the SDA that sent people to Croatia for training. Their number was significant. There must have between 6.000 and 10.000 people. I don't know how many, but their number was great. At the end of the day, there are documents to corroborate that. When they returned from Croatia, they created huge problems.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 1D5690.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is an intercept of a conversation involving myself and vice-president Koljevic and the conversation took place on the 20th of June. I'm interested in page 1 in English, towards the bottom of the page where it says: "I can't get in touch with Zepinic to see if he knows. The MUP sent 2.000 Muslims to the Pionirski town in Zagreb." That was before 20th June, and there were more of them after the 20th, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know one part of the situation, but -- and I want to share with you that part of the information. In the Ministry of Interior --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Not only is this leading, but it appears to me to be going beyond the scope of my cross-examination. I certainly didn't go into all of these issues regarding 1991 and the formation of any Muslim or non-Serb units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You didn't rise when -- during the previous question and answer, just -- and therefore, I let it go. Why don't you -- why don't we allow him to continue. Yes, please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It appeared to be leading, but the minister had just said that he was aware of several thousand of people who were sent. Here I say that there were 2.000 before the 20th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please continue?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to be very fair, and I want to say this: The MUP of the former Bosnia and Herzegovina was where the former SDA appointed an assistant minister. He was a Muslim priest who had arrived from Zagreb. And it wasn't the MUP but he personally, and I don't know how he introduced himself there, he personally took care of that but it was the Party of Democratic Action that sent those people and their number was much greater than it says here. It may have been so -- that many up to that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the following page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here, I am asking Mr. Koljevic about the arms that had arrived in Prijedor. Did -- were you aware of that, that there was an arming drive in June 1991?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had some general information about people being armed. I mentioned that yesterday. I didn't have any specific information about Prijedor. I was more interested in SUP of the city of Sarajevo. So except for some general information, I can't share with you anything specific.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this intercept be admitted and marked for identification, like the other intercepts before this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D4284, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that not -- that Serbs were not appointed to each and every position that they got, especially in state security. Did I ask for agreements to be abided by?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you by way of my general knowledge. But I know that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Well, leading, Your Honours. And top of that, again, this isn't anything I went into on cross-examination. This was a topic of direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I agree with you. I tend to agree with you. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer? The reasons were the divisions. The Prosecution implied that it was our fault that the MUP was divided. So now we are presenting the reasons why we asked the European Union for our entity to have its own police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure I ...

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I'm not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm not sure that that was what I was getting into on cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, the cross-examination was to the effect that the Serbs had divided the MUP as part of their plan to take control of Serb areas and force Muslims and Croats to be expelled. Now Dr. Karadzic is trying to show the reasons why the MUP were divided, and I think it's within the cross-examination and he should be allowed to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Robinson. Yes, please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 17561.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please focus on this document. I'm writing a letter to the Presidency of the Bosnia and to the president for -- president of the council for the protection of the constitutional order. I am saying that agreements had not been carried out and also that there was no proportion of representation of peoples in state organs. Is that what you said? How does this fit into your own knowledge about the functioning?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A moment ago, I said that by way of general knowledge, I was aware of all of these problems. I know that through Momcilo Mandic and Vitomir Zepinic, you tried to obtain information and that you insisted that, in accordance with the agreement, personnel be appointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D4285, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In relation to the same topic but also in terms of your relations with me, yesterday the Prosecutor suggested that I addressed you by your first name, meaning that we were on "tu" terms. Were we on "tu" or "vous" terms?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never the informal "tu." It was always official, our communication. And you and I never had a cup of coffee together on our own.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please take a look at 65 ter 31863.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The fourth line from the bottom, is it correct that I'm asking, Is this the Stanisic apartment? So does that mean that I called you?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Next page, please. The English was ... oh. Please, we are talking, and I'm going to read out the first longer part -- well, look, we're angry with the MUP and I'm cussing and I'm saying, I don't know if you know that they are mistreating our people. I don't know whether it's your people from the city MUP. But it is amazing -- It would be the next page in English. But it's amazing what they're doing, how much effort they're making to follow our people and to suspect them of all sorts of things. And then further down, it says: "Please tell Mandic" -- [In English] Next page in English, please. [Interpretation] Oh, it's here, Mandic. I'm asking you to tell Mandic that we have enough evidence to turn that MUP upside down and to hand them over to the army and the federal MUP so that they could arrest them. So what is all this about? Why would we report them to the army and the federal MUP?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you've put two questions to me. First, address. I'm looking at this transcript now. When you reached me on the phone, you said, Comrade secretary. Radovan Karadzic, How are you? And I say, Fine. And how are you? This is the -- 1, 2, 3, 4. It is paragraph 5, 6, and 7 from the topic of this page which is on my screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I understand, Minister. But, in English it's just you regardless of whether it is "vous" or "tu" and that's why I say this led the Prosecutor to --

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, no. In Serbian or the Serbo-Croat language, "vous" and "tu," there is a great difference in terms of these forms of address. T is one person. V is just an address of courtesy. Otherwise it's the plural. So then when you are addressing a person, with whom you do not have any kind of informal relationship, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: French-speaking people understand what you are saying, and I believe that others have understood by now. Why am I saying that they -- that they should be reported, that we would report them to the federal MUP and to the army?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, precisely, as far as I can see on the basis of this content, because of the problems that we spoke of a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now you said there that there was that wide-spread anti-army feeling, federal regulations.

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The army was a symbol of the unity of the former Yugoslavia; that is to say, it was the only state organ of the federal state that was a single one without being subdivided in the republics. Everything was done to break that last organ up as well so that this principle of separation could be exercised, the one that they were aspiring for.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, page 4, please, and the next one in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the second line here, you're saying that we should wait a bit, that you should check this. And I say, All right. Just because of you, we will be waiting. And we have enough information for Alija Delimustafic, Hilmo Selimovic and Avdo Hebib, enough to give them hell.

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So what is the question? Could you just tell me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The question is why you were being so cautious. Why did you want to check?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You spoke about problems in the territory of the city of Sarajevo where I was secretary of the secretariat and, of course, I would say that everything had to be checked so that a final conclusion could be reached in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about these three that I mentioned, who are they? The ones that I mentioned that we have --

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you just tell me where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Alija Delimustafic, Hilmo Selimovic, Avdo Hebib.

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, there was information then that Avdo Hebib, in particular, was arming the Muslim people through the reserve force throughout the former Bosnia-Herzegovina. And there were a lot of Official Notes that were coming in from the field in this respect and they were providing information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I draw your attention to this central part: Because I think, et cetera. The Prosecutor suggested that you were being controlled by the SDS and Karadzic and look at this sentence: We do not know exactly what the situation is in the city SUP because we have not quite focussed on that but we do have all the information, et cetera. What can you say about that?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I, as secretary of the city SUP, protected the interest of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: It's leading, Your Honours. It's within the scope of my cross-examination, but it's -- it's certainly leading. And because it is dealing with a different topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, again, I don't see anything wrong with putting a document or a portion of a document and asking, What can you say about that? I cannot think of anything less leading than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Except for, Your Honour, that Mr. Karadzic prefaced it with what I was dealing with during cross-examination and then obviously trying to tie it to something said during this conversation. And that, in itself, is extremely leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this time we agree with Mr. Olmsted. Move on or reformulate your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, I didn't even have to put this question because Mr. Stanisic denied during the cross-examination that he was under anybody's control. But let's move on. Let's move on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: During this conversation, you tried to calm me down and to delay matters. Look at this, Fine, fine, fine. Just take a look at this. What is it that I'm asking you? It's page 6 in English.

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can only conclude that, over here -- how I do put this? - you lowered your expectations. You asked for less. Just to inform people at the MUP that this has gone way too far.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you trying to say that I yielded to you?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But at the beginning of this conversation --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Never mind. I'm not ashamed of this. I am willing to accept arguments, reasoning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D4286, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The previous page, lines 18 and 19, you mentioned Avdo Hebib. What was his formal position in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Avdo Hebib, but a lot before me, was an advisor, special advisor to the minister of Bosnia-Herzegovina for public security affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I mentioned him as one of the three persons that we were objecting to.

utterances.speaker: MICO STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 31914. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, this is the 17th of September, so it's a week after that public release. Then I'm speaking to Mr. Hebib. So could I have the next page both in Serbian and in English. Mr. Hebib says, and that's the penultimate part, and he says that he doesn't want to have anything to do with national parties. And then I said that everybody came to power through the political parties. And I am saying that there is a proportionate government: 43 for the Muslims, 35.6 for the Serbs, and so on. You see? Tonight I have got a definite conversation with Mr. Izetbegovic and I'm going to ask that several people be thrown out of the MUP because they are leading Bosnia and Herzegovina - can we have the next page in Serbian - into a civil war because what we had agreed upon is not being respected. Mr. Hebib, there cannot be any lateral appointments in the MUP anymore, neither can the Serbs appoint staff to the Muslims nor the Muslims to the Serbs and there can especially be no such one-sided changes. If we've agreed about everything from start to finish, then we also have to agree about how much, what structure, and who is going where. And it's the ruling party that has to say that. Now, how does this fit into what you knew about the position of the SDS in respect of having these problems resolved?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, leading for the reasons I have raised before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not sure I really even know what is a leading question anymore. But Dr. Karadzic already raised the topic with Minister Stanisic. He has asked him several questions about the reason for the splitting of the MUP and the conflict and now he is putting to him a specific example and asked him what he thinks about it or to comment on it. I simply don't see how that could possibly be leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
